purpose: Resolve dusk/night track decay, Japanese land-based night-strike restraint, US runway-denial maneuver, and the pre-dawn carrier-scout contact that opens the first-line carrier GO gate.

events.event: US cruisers/destroyers continue intermittent runway/radar denial at Taroa/Wotje while carrier TGs move their night stations and strengthen CAP/ASW after repeated submarine contact. Japanese water-air scouts attempt one dusk refresh but cannot hold a carrier visual through CAP/weather.
events.result: The 13:00 carrier track ages; no dusk weapon solution.

events.event: Combined Fleet declines a second mass land-based night torpedo attack. Eniwetok and scattered attack aircraft are retained primarily as emergency search/harassment reserve; two low-signature reconnaissance/area-check sorties generate no firm carrier visual.
events.reason: With only ~62 local serviceable aircraft at 16:30, another 4-8 aircraft torpedo raid has lower expected value than preserving the cue/confirm chain for the three fleet carriers.

events.event: Two submarine nodes produce intermittent hydrophone/escort contacts on the predicted carrier/support corridor. Neither can classify a carrier or maintain shadow under US patrol pressure.
events.knowledge: MEDIUM same operational axis; position uncertainty expands to roughly 60-90 nmi by midnight.

events.event: US TG58.2 executes high-speed night displacement with zig-zag and limited course change while TG58.1/58.3 remain separated by their target/support responsibilities. Japanese HQ treats the old track as a search corridor, not a firing solution.
Shokaku/Zuikaku/Hiryu launch an eight-aircraft pre-dawn carrier reconnaissance fan while closing to the precomputed launch/recovery gate. Scouts are separate from the later strike count.
events.assets: D4Y/B6N reconnaissance mix; no magical radar search.

events.event: One scout reacquires the same three-deck/three-fast-battleship group about 220-250 nmi east-southeast of the Japanese carrier force. Launch/recovery activity is visible.
events.confidence: HIGH TG58.2-class fresh target; position error about 10-15 nmi at report time.

events.event: A second scout obtains a shorter visual on another US carrier group roughly 140-180 nmi north/northeast of the primary target. The third group remains sector-level only.
events.effect: Japan now has enough two-group geometry to know the primary group is not physically merged with the other fast decks, while still accepting counterstrike risk.

events.event: GO gate opens. The primary TG is fresh, visibly mission-split by launch activity, launch/recovery range is acceptable, and the Japanese force has a westward egress.

anti_overreach: No shore-water aircraft magically guides the carrier strike continuously
Second US TG visual is enough for separation geometry, not a full 11-deck OOB
GO is an informed risk decision, not knowledge that the other US groups cannot counterstrike
